title: SKU-aligned capacity planning and price-scan (Apr 2026)
body:
PURPOSE
Quick-run financial model and operational playbook that maps product SKUs (hosted tiers + dedicated plans) to GPU capacity buckets, associates a hiring ladder to fill gaps, and runs a compact price-elasticity scan to show coverage and burn impact for Q2–Q4 2026. This is a working sheet intended for the finance + product pricing sync before a more formal deck.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
- Objective: ensure SKU coverage >= 95% for forecasted demand under base and mild-upside scenarios while keeping incremental gross margin impact < 4 percentage points.
- Key levers: per-SKU price delta, commit vs burst mix, hiring cadence for infra and SRE, and short-term leased GPU hours.
- Recommendation (working): keep hosted API prices unchanged; introduce a micro-tier surcharge for high-throughput SKUs and accelerate hiring by two engineers in July if demand realization > 110% of baseline.

ASSUMPTIONS
- Time horizon: Apr 2026 -> Dec 2026.
- Baseline traffic growth: 6% month-over-month from existing customer base.
- SKU definitions: Free, Starter, Team, Scale, Dedicated-S1, Dedicated-S2.
- Unit: GPU-hours per 100k tokens at 4k context window (derived from serving runtime bench v2.1).
- Elasticity: assumed price elasticity of demand by SKU: Free: -0.10, Starter: -0.25, Team: -0.40, Scale: -0.55, Dedicated: -0.15 (commit-heavy).
- Hiring ramp: typical hire lead time = 8 weeks; effective capacity contribution per infra engineer hire = ~6 reserved-GPU-hours/day in steady state after bootstrapping.
- Short-term leases: available in 1-week blocks with 48-hour lead time at 1.6x standard spot cost.

SHEET: SKUs -> capacity mapping (monthly view)
Columns: SKU | Baseline Users | Avg qps per user | Token/month per user | GPU-hours/100k tokens | Est GPU-hours/month | Apr-Jun demand | Jul-Sep demand | Oct-Dec demand | Notes
Row: Free | 24,000 | 0.04 | 75k | 2.2 | 3,960 | 4,200 (base+6% m/m) | 4,460 | 4,740 | low rev, monitoring only
Row: Starter | 6,200 | 0.12 | 220k | 1.8 | 2,462 | 2,612 | 2,780 | 2,960 | price-sensitive
Row: Team | 1,400 | 0.45 | 850k | 1.3 | 1,157 | 1,227 | 1,302 | 1,382 | key expansion SKU
Row: Scale | 360 | 1.8 | 3.2M | 0.9 | 1,036 | 1,099 | 1,166 | 1,238 | high throughput, elastic
Row: Dedicated-S1 | 45 | NA | reserved commit | N/A | reserved block | reserved | reserved | reserved | capacity contracted
Row: Dedicated-S2 | 22 | NA | reserved commit | N/A | reserved block | reserved | reserved | reserved | enterprise heavy

HEADCOUNT HIRING LADDER (Q2–Q4 2026)
- Current open reqs (as of 2026-04-12): 3 infra eng, 2 SRE, 1 finance analyst (contract).
- Proposed ladder: May (close 1 infra + 1 SRE), Jun (close 1 infra), Jul (accelerate: close 1 infra + 1 SRE), Sep (evaluate need for 1 product ops).
- Capacity model: each infra hire yields +180 GPU-hours/month after 8-week onboarding; each SRE hire yields +90 GPU-hours/month via operational efficiency improvements in month 3 post-hire.
- Burn impact: all hires fully ramped by Oct -> incremental OTE run-rate = $1.02M ARR (annualized salary+burden).

PRICING SENSITIVITY SCAN (compact)
Scenario columns: Scenario | Price change (%) per SKU | Elasticity applied | Net revenue delta | Demand delta | Unit cost delta | Gross margin delta
Base scenario | 0% | n/a | 0 | 0% | 0 | 0 p.p.
Mild up | +6% on Scale only | elasticity -0.55 | +4.2% revenue | -3.3% demand on Scale | -0.9% unit cost | +1.8 p.p.
Protect margin | +12% on Team+Scale | team -0.40, scale -0.55 | +9.6% revenue | -6.8% aggregated demand | -1.6% unit cost | +3.4 p.p.
Elastic shock | -8% across hosted SKUs | avg elasticity -0.35 | -6.2% revenue | +2.9% demand | +2.0% unit cost | -2.9 p.p.
Commit tilt | shift 8% of Scale usage to Dedicated commit plans (introduce small discount) | modeled sticky | -2.1% revenue (short) | -9.4% demand on hosted | -6.8% unit cost | +2.9 p.p.

COVERAGE & CAPACITY GAP SUMMARY (base vs mild-upside)
- Base baseline capacity need (Apr-Jun): 13.6k GPU-hours/month. On-hand capacity (reserved + existing spot) = 12.0k -> gap = 1.6k.
- If mild-upside (+20% demand spike): gap = 3.8k.
- Hiring ladder (as proposed) closes ~1.1k by Sep (phased); remaining gap covered by short-term leases and commit reshuffle.

DECISION TRIGGERS (operational playbook)
- Trigger A: Weekly usage > baseline +7% for three consecutive weeks -> start 1-week short-term lease (72 hours lead) and open expedited contractor search.
- Trigger B: Realized revenue per token falls > 5% QoQ and hosted utilization > 85% -> pricing A/B test to raise Scale tier by +8% for new customers, keep existing customers on stable pricing; evaluate migration uplift after 6 weeks.
- Trigger C: Sales signals (2+ enterprise deals with Dedicated interest) -> shift 10% of forecasted Scale capacity into Dedicated commit conversion reserve; finance to model revenue timing.

RISK NOTES
- Elasticity uncertainty: small sample set for Scale tier; if actual elasticity magnitude < assumed (i.e., less price-sensitive), recommended price increases would yield more revenue but risk churn in adjacent SMB accounts.
- Hiring timing: market may push lead times >8 weeks in Aug -> contingency: convert one infra req to contractor for Q3 spike.
- Measurement noise: streaming billing and fractional token accounting introduces ~±3% measurement variance month-to-month; smooth with 4-week moving average for triggers.

ACTIONS / NEXT STEPS
- Finance to produce a 13-week cash/usage overlay by Apr 30 (owner: Maya).
- Product + Sales to confirm whether two inbound enterprise prospects will sign Dedicated-S1 by May 10 (owner: Priya).
- Growth to run a 2-arm pricing A/B for Scale new signups starting Jun 1 (owner: Diego).
- Ops to validate short-lease pricing and procurement SLA with cloud partners (owner: Liam).

APPENDIX: CALCULATION SNIPPETS (for verification)
- GPU-hours/month = (users * tokens_per_user_per_month / 100,000) * GPU-hours/100k_tokens.
- Example: Scale Apr -> 360 * 3.2M/100k * 0.9 = 360 * 32 * 0.9 = 10,368 GPU-hours/year -> 864 GPU-hours/month (numbers in sheet rounded).

NOTES TO SELF (informal)
- Need to sync with serving-runtime on the latest bench v2.2 kernels; numbers above use v2.1 (ask @akshat).
- Re-run elasticity estimates after Growth finishes the micro-A/B in May.
- Potential clean-up: move the SKU mapping into a canonical cost-model repo and link the canonical sheet id here.

REVISION HISTORY
- 2026-04-12: initial draft (Maya).
- 2026-04-18: added hiring ladder and short-lease options (Diego).
- 2026-04-25: tightened triggers, added commit-tilt scenario (Priya).

END OF SHEET
